summary: The service started this run, not an instruction. It was triggered because two width-200 baseline loops ended (jobs 164689 and 164690, f* 0.50 and 0.44, unmodified engine with friction). There were no Asked items, so nothing could go unanswered. No claims were proposed or changed, and no claims or blockers are open on this line. I checked the run's numbers against the raw outputs. For both new loops I matched every per-step entry in evidence/E0076-interim.json to its mirrored summary.json by SHA-256. That covers forty-nine steps for f* 0.50 and forty-seven for f* 0.44, checking Gamma, outcome, cycles, CPU-hours, energy gains, audit failures and slow episodes. There were zero mismatches. The ranges reproduce: f* 0.50 covered Gamma 2.35 to 4.0 and f* 0.44 covered 2.4 to 4.0. So do the stops: CPU-cap stops at 2.3 and 2.35 (2.004 and 2.007 CPU-hours against a two CPU-hour cap) and sphere overlaps at 4.05. The step-cost medians (1.071 and 1.148 CPU-hours) and step sums (56.55 and 56.52, against 56.89 and 56.85 in the job records) match. No step gained energy, failed the audit or had a slow stretch, so the referee check on slow_episodes is clean: these loops never slowed down. The run answered my challenge from earlier today. I fetched four width-100 ramp.jsonl files from A0068. Their SHA-256 match the new width100_stop_modes table, and their stop outcomes match it. At f* 0.57, 0.50 and 0.44 the floor was a CPU-cap stop at both widths, as the run now says. I recomputed the down-leg cost ratio myself and got the same forty-nine pairs, from 6.63 to 8.40 with a median of 7.42. The differences are only in the second decimal and come from rounding. The line state's comparisons hold. f* 0.65 has overlaps at both ends at both widths: 2.4 to 3.9 against 2.25 to 4.1. At f* 0.57 the top is a stall at 3.85 against an overlap at 4.05. At f* 0.44 the top is an overlap against a stall at 4.05, so both reach 4.0. The state rightly leaves out the f* 0.50 top, because the width-100 top there was a cap stop. Its counts are also right: nine of thirty loops ended, and four of the ten baseline loops broke on their first step while four finished. My smaller earlier points were fixed too. 'Five to seven times' was replaced by the measured figure, and the timestamps (15:26:31) now fall before the commit (15:27:51) instead of after it. Three things need correcting, none serious. (1) The L0018 line note and the session headline say 'a step costs about 7.4 times as much at width 200'. That figure was measured only on the way down, below Gamma 3.0. On the way up, above Gamma 3.0, I get medians of 11.5 at f* 0.44, 11.4 at f* 0.57, 6.8 at f* 0.50 and 7.4 at f* 0.65 over sixteen to twenty pairs each. The up-leg cap was also scaled four times (2.0 to 8.0 CPU-hours), so a top that stops on the cap is even less comparable than a floor that does. No top compared so far was a width-200 cap stop. But f* 0.74 and 0.84 had width-100 tops that were cap stops, and those loops are next to be compared. The line state sentence itself is worded correctly ('a 25-cycle step below Gamma 3.0'). The fix is to say 'on the way down' in the note, and to add the up-leg ratio to down_leg_cost_ratio or beside it before the E0076 outcome table is written. (2) The experiment text says the f* 0.50 overlap at 4.05 came 'in the first cycle' and the f* 0.44 one 'in cycle sixteen'. In referee/long_contact.py, failure_cycle is sim.cycle, the number of cycles already completed. The f* 0.50 failure therefore came after one full cycle, in the second, and the f* 0.44 one in the seventeenth. The run's earlier write-up of the 3.85 stall counted cycles the other way (10 completed, 'cycle 11'). (3) The weekly budget figure (561.44 of 10000, 6 percent) leaves out the two jobs that just ended, about 114 CPU-hours. The run says so itself. With them it is about 675, or 7 percent. program check passes. It lists three approvals in the last day (Nov 23 15:47 and 15:49, and Nov 24 03:19). I reported all three before, and whether they were Chris's is for Chris to confirm. sequel-data is 647 megabytes against a 15 gigabyte ceiling. Free disk is 91 gigabytes against a 40 gigabyte floor. tmp/ is empty: I deleted my own fetch of four ramp.jsonl files. I found nothing written outside the two allowed folders in the run's window except the harness's own files. No time went to unasked work. As the user instructed, this review is committed on branch line/L0018 in the line's worktree, not on main.

run_conditions.assessment: This was a four-minute service run. The job records were committed at 15:22:54. The run says it started at 15:23:58 and ended at 15:27:21, and its commit is at 15:27:51. It only read fetched outputs, so the zero local CPU-hours it recorded is right. Twenty-one of thirty width-200 loops are still running on Hatteras: ten E0074, nine E0075 and two E0076. None was started, cancelled or restarted. active.jsonl is empty, which is correct for cluster jobs. The host is a Linux container, so pmset and uptime are unavailable and sleep could not be measured, and the summary says so. Free disk was 91 gigabytes, as recorded. The machine did not limit the science. The loops' own CPU caps set the floors, and the run now says so plainly.
discrepancies: scheduled_start (15:22:47Z) is the end time of the second job, not a measured runner start, as the summary itself admits.
